item.title: Celtics overcome 20-point deficit to top Pacers 103-95
item.description: Jaylen Brown scored 31 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, to lead the Boston Celtics to a 103-95 comeback victory over the Indiana Pacers, who lost their fifth straight game.

item.title: IMPD seeks help locating 13-year-old boy last seen on Indy’s east side
item.description: The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department is asking for the public's help to find a 13-year-old boy last seen at an apartment complex on Sunday.

item.title: Boston grandma receives $30 Barbie from Canada, then $802 tariff charge from shipper
item.description: A woman received an $802 invoice for a $30 Barbie doll due to a decimal point error, highlighting the added costs and complex paperwork of the Trump Administration's tariffs and the elimination of the de minimis exemption.

item.title: Woman dies after assault on Indy’s far east side
item.description: A woman is in critical condition after being assaulted at an apartment complex in Indianapolis, and police are investigating the incident.

item.title: Colts lose fifth straight game, fall to 49ers
item.description: The Colts lost to the 49ers 48-27, dropping their record to 8-7 and marking their fifth consecutive loss.

item.title: Carmel man charged in I-465 road rage case
item.description: Thomas Wayne Ferguson, 37, of Carmel, Indiana, was charged with multiple felony counts after a road rage incident on I-465 that led to a report of shots being fired.

item.title: Florida fugitive apprehended after standoff in Avon housing subdivision
item.description: An 18-year-old man wanted in Florida was taken into custody after a standoff with police on Monday afternoon in a residential subdivision in Avon, Indiana, in which he fired shots at an armored vehicle.

item.title: Driver dies after collision on Arlington Avenue in Indianapolis
item.description: A person died after a two-car crash on Indianapolis' east side Monday afternoon, and investigators believe the deceased driver may have suffered from a medical issue before the crash.

item.title: Former Indy nonprofit CEO pleads guilty to wire fraud after stealing over $2M from business
item.description: Theresa Szwast, the former CEO of an Indianapolis-based nonprofit, has been sentenced to 33 months in prison and a $5,000 fine for embezzling over $2 million from the organization for personal expenses.

item.title: Downtown Indianapolis bar raises age limit to from 21 to 30
item.description: Georgia Street Rhythm & Blues Lounge in downtown Indianapolis has raised its age restriction to 30 and older, due to younger patrons not knowing how to conduct themselves in the environment.
